Subject: Three-model recommendation + bench links & prompt-set (post-demo)

Hey Claire + Devon — thanks again for the demo time this morning. Below is a concise post-demo recommendation and immediate asks so we can get a pilot scheduled. TL;DR: three candidate models with recommended roles, plus links to the benchmark CSV, the prompt set we used, and a short pilot evaluation plan.

Recommended candidate slate (rationale in-line):

1) rw-7b-v2-int8 (recommended start for chat/interactive routing)
   - Why: best-in-class latency and cost for turn-by-turn conversational workloads when quantized (INT8).
   - Tradeoffs: slightly lower long-context synthesis quality vs larger engines; very low p95 latency (we measured ~55ms/token on g4-like hardware for your prompt mix).

2) rw-13b-q4 (balanced workhorse for summarization / multi-turn extraction)
   - Why: strong factuality and synthesis vs 7B, with moderate cost. Good default for summarization and longer prompts.
   - Tradeoffs: higher memory footprint; p95 latency ~120ms/token in our hosted runs, but still within sub-second response for typical WalkerAI queries.

3) open-llama-30b-gguf (quality-optimized fallback for heavy reasoning and overnight batch jobs)
   - Why: best raw quality in our public-catalog tests for the kinds of multi-paragraph synthesis you care about.
   - Tradeoffs: cost and latency are higher; better used for async batch or gated escalation paths.

Attachments & links sent: walker_bench_20280719.csv (bench details by prompt category), walker_prompt_set_v1.txt (the prompt bundles I used in the demo), pilot-eval-plan-RA-202807.pdf (proposed 3-week pilot with eval criteria). Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDEF-DriveLink-walkerai

Suggested next steps (short):
- You pick priority use case(s) for the 3-week pilot (chat routing + summarization is our recommended trio).
- We run a 7-day narrow pilot (rw-7b-v2-int8 hosted) to validate latency/cost under your traffic profile.
- Parallel A/B slot: rw-13b-q4 for a subset of heavy summarization tasks.
- Metrics: p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, hallucination rate (manual sample), and task-based accuracy (we propose a 200-example eval set in the attached plan).

Operational asks:
- Claire: can you share an anonymized 24-hour sample of traffic for a realistic pilot (headers/token distributions)?
- Devon: which SLA/latency band are you targeting (p95 < 300ms, p95 < 200ms, etc.)?

I’ll sync with Ben/Karthik/Monica internally to map pilot capacity and provide a pricing sketch. If you’re happy with this slate, I can set up a 30-min pilot kickoff next week.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Quick answers below; Ben/Monica/Karthik please weigh in on infra/pricing details.

Pricing (approx cost per 1M tokens, hosted API sketch):
- rw-7b-v2-int8: ~$45 / 1M tokens (hosted, INT8 runtime) — lowest cost path for chat.
- rw-13b-q4: ~$130 / 1M tokens (balanced quality/cost).
- open-llama-30b-gguf: ~$420 / 1M tokens (quality-optimized; consider for async).

Latency at 200rps peak (approx, hosted with continuous-batching + prefix cache):
- rw-7b-v2-int8: expected p95 for 30-token responses ~300–400ms if served on shared hosted capacity at that scale; with Dedicated/Reserved pool this drops to ~120–180ms p95.
- rw-13b-q4: p95 ~600–800ms on hosted; Dedicated reduces to ~220–330ms.
- open-llama-30b-gguf: p95 >1.5s on hosted; Dedicated/optimized infra needed for sub-second.

Regression monitoring (short):
- We include continuous evals on your seeded prompt set (attached) plus a rolling sample of production traffic. Signal types: semantic-drift (embedding cosine shift vs baseline), hallucination-rate (human-labeled sample), and task-accuracy (automated checks where possible).
- Alerting: thresholded alerts (e.g., hallucination spike >2x baseline) routed to your CS + our ML Ops channel; automatic canary rollback to previous model version is supported.
- We note this in the pilot-eval-plan (see section 2). If you want, Karthik can add concrete alert thresholds and a sample Grafana dashboard.

Ben / Monica / Karthik: can someone produce a pricing sketch for Dedicated reserve vs hosted run at the volumes Claire mentioned? We can put both on the pilot decision doc.

Thanks — Rafael

Rafael et al — quick ops note and numbers from the infra bench runs (summarized):

- rw-7b-v2-int8: on a 4xA10g Dedicated pool with continuous batching we see sustained 200rps serving 30-token responses with p95 ~140–170ms (matching Rafael's Dedicated estimate). At peak burst factors >2x we'd recommend autoscale policy with 20% burst buffer.
- rw-13b-q4: 8xA10g pool gives p95 ~240–300ms for same profile when pinned (higher memory but good throughput).
- open-llama-30b-gguf: needs 4xH100 or optimized 8xA100-style infra to keep p95 under 1s; cost footprint is significant.

Ops controls we recommend for WalkerAI pilot:
1) Enable prefix KV caching for repeated conversational threads (reduces token compute by ~20–35%).
2) Configure a short-term cache for summary artifacts (TTL ~1h) to avoid re-generating identical summaries.
3) Canary rollout: start with 5% traffic to rw-13b-q4 for summarization, 95% to rw-7b-v2-int8 for chat; evaluate metrics at 48h.

Also added a small script to the Drive folder that calculates estimated monthly spend for given RPS / avg tokens per response. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDEF-DriveLink-walkerai (see spend-estimator.csv).
